operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are backtick-quoted in DDL; generated SQL must double-quote them ("Ref_Colors") — sqlite accepts both, but the writer must not copy backticks into double-quote contexts.
Table/column names are mixed-case with underscores (Ref_Characteristic_Types, product_category_code); case-insensitive lookup required, original spelling preserved.
Tiny tables: Ref_Characteristic_Types=2, Ref_Product_Categories=3, Ref_Colors=8 rows; parent pools are smaller than typical child sizes, so FK draws with replacement will repeat heavily.
Product_Characteristics has NO primary key (pk=[]) — sample_fresh_primary_keys must be a no-op there; drop_unique_duplicates also no-op (no unique cols).
typical_buying_price / typical_selling_price are VARCHAR(20) but store numeric-looking text ('352447.2874677', '5.578', '') — declared type dispatches to String fuzzer, not Number.
typical_buying_price has an empty-string sample ('') — String fuzzer's int-like branch and contaminate must tolerate ''.
other_characteristic_details and other_product_details are 100% NULL (distinct=0, storage=['null']) — original_values are all None; Base drops None so sampler falls back to p=1 fresh strings.
unit_of_measure sample 'Handful             ' has trailing spaces (VARCHAR(20) padding) — String length range will include 20.
color_code values are digit-strings ('1'..'8') but declared VARCHAR — String fuzzer's int-like branch will add str(i±1) neighbors, producing '0','9' etc. that don't exist in Ref_Colors.
characteristic_data_type has 15 distinct values on 15 rows (near-unique) but is not declared UNIQUE — no dedup enforced.
All FKs point to existing parents with unique PKs; no dangling FKs, no self-references, no composite keys.

Products.color_code NOT NULL and product_category_code NOT NULL; Characteristics.characteristic_type_code NOT NULL; Product_Characteristics both FK cols NOT NULL — NULL FK draws from empty parent would fail insert and be skipped.
operator_ts_expectations: All VARCHAR columns -> String fuzzer (charset a-zA-Z 0-9(), length range from samples, contaminate 0.5).
INTEGER PKs (characteristic_id, product_id) -> Number fuzzer scale=0, int perturbation ±1/±2; fresh draws uniform in [-1,1] then int-perturbed — will collide with existing small ints.

Ref_Colors.color_code String fuzzer sees digit-strings '1'..'8', adds '0','9','10' etc. via int-like branch — FK children may draw these, but parent pool is the FINAL filtered Ref_Colors.color_code so only real values propagate.
Ref_Characteristic_Types has only 2 rows; Characteristics.characteristic_type_code FK draws from {Grade,Purity} with replacement — heavy duplication, but NOT NULL so no NULLs.

Product_Characteristics has no PK and no unique cols -> no dedup; product_id/characteristic_id drawn from parent final pools (9 distinct each) with replacement -> many duplicate (product_id,characteristic_id) pairs, which is fine (no constraint).

other_*_details columns: original_values all None -> Base drops -> p=1 -> pure fresh random strings of length 0..20 (or 0..255 from VARCHAR(255) arg? — String uses args[0] or 20, so VARCHAR(255) gives length 255).
typical_*_price String fuzzer: samples include '' and long decimals; length range [0, max_len+1]; int-like branch fires on '39446' adding '39445','39447'.

Likely FN driver: String fuzzer produces garbage for product_name/description that no gold query filters on, so predicates like product_name='cumin' return empty in generated instances -> gold and candidate both empty -> no kill.
Likely FP driver: Number fuzzer on INTEGER PKs produces small ints (-1,0,1,2) that collide with real PKs; joins on product_id may match spuriously.
Ref_Product_Categories.unit_of_measure has 2 distinct values with trailing spaces — String fuzzer preserves length range up to 20, contaminate may strip/append.
No Date/Time/Bool columns in this DB — those fuzzers never fire.
Table sizes: choose_table_sizes will give Ref_* tables 1..2500 rows (level 0) and children 4x — but FK draws from tiny parent pools mean effective distinctness is capped at 2/3/8.
